chapters.1.summary: Elkanah has two wives, and Hannah has no children. Each year at Shiloh the other wife taunts her until she weeps. Hannah prays in bitter grief and vows to give a son to the LORD. Eli the priest sees her lips move and thinks she is drunk. She explains, and he sends her away with a blessing. She bears a son and names him Samuel. When he is weaned she brings him to Eli at Shiloh. She gives him to the LORD for his whole life.
chapters.1.lds: The Church lesson studies Hannah's prayer during grief and her trust in God. How does Hannah answer Eli in verses 15–16?
chapters.2.summary: Hannah sings that the LORD brings down the strong and lifts the poor. Eli’s sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are priests who do not know the LORD. They take the best meat by force before the fat is burned. They also sleep with women who serve at the tent door. Eli rebukes them, but they do not listen. Meanwhile the boy Samuel grows and serves before the LORD. A man of God tells Eli that his house will lose the priesthood. Both sons will die on one day.
chapters.2.lds: The older Church manual connects Hannah's song with Jesus Christ. What does the man of God say Eli has honored above the LORD (verse 29)?
chapters.3.summary: The boy Samuel serves under Eli, and words from the LORD are rare. One night a voice calls Samuel, and he runs to Eli. This happens three times before Eli understands. He tells Samuel to answer, “Speak, LORD, for your servant hears.” The LORD says he will judge Eli’s house for the sons’ sin. Eli knew and did not restrain them. In the morning Samuel is afraid, but Eli makes him tell everything. All Israel learns that Samuel is a prophet.
chapters.3.lds: Come, Follow Me connects Samuel’s response with learning to recognize revelation. Who teaches Samuel how to answer the voice (verses 8–9)?
chapters.4.summary: Israel fights the Philistines and loses four thousand men. The elders send to Shiloh for the ark of the covenant. Hophni and Phinehas come with it, and the camp shouts. The Philistines are afraid but urge each other to fight like men. Israel loses thirty thousand men, the ark is captured, and Eli’s sons die. A runner brings the news to Shiloh. Eli falls from his seat and dies when he hears about the ark. His daughter-in-law dies in childbirth and names her son Ichabod.
chapters.4.lds: The Church lesson examines trust in the ark. Why does carrying the ark fail to protect the army?
chapters.5.summary: The Philistines bring the ark to Ashdod and set it beside their god Dagon. The next morning Dagon’s statue lies face down before the ark. They set it up, and the next day it has fallen again. Its head and hands lie broken on the threshold. The LORD strikes Ashdod with tumors. The people send the ark to Gath, and the same thing happens. Gath sends it to Ekron, and Ekron cries out in terror. The city’s cry goes up to heaven.
chapters.5.lds: The older manual connects the ark’s troubles with Israel’s need to honor God. What do the men of Ashdod conclude in verse 7?
chapters.6.summary: After seven months the Philistines ask their priests how to send the ark back. The priests advise a guilt offering of five golden tumors and five golden mice. They warn the people not to harden their hearts as Egypt did. They hitch two milk cows to a new cart and pen up the calves. If the cows go toward Israel, the LORD sent the plague. The cows walk straight to Beth Shemesh, lowing as they go. The people there rejoice and offer the cows. Some look into the ark and die, and the town sends it away.
chapters.6.lds: The Church lesson uses these events to study trust and obedience. Why do the Philistines use cows that have calves at home (verses 7–9)?
chapters.7.summary: The ark stays at Kiriath Jearim for twenty years. Samuel tells Israel to put away foreign gods and serve the LORD alone. They do so and gather at Mizpah to fast and confess. The Philistines hear of the gathering and attack. The people beg Samuel to keep praying for them. He offers a lamb, and the LORD thunders against the Philistines. Israel chases them, and Samuel sets up a stone named Ebenezer. Samuel judges Israel on a yearly circuit from his home in Ramah.
chapters.7.lds: Come, Follow Me studies turning toward God after earlier failure. What does Israel do in verses 3–6 before the battle?
chapters.8.summary: Samuel grows old, and his sons take bribes as judges. The elders ask him for a king like all the nations have. Samuel is displeased and prays. The LORD says the people have rejected him, not Samuel, as king. Samuel must warn them how a king will behave. A king will take their sons, daughters, fields, crops, servants, and flocks. They will cry out, and the LORD will not answer. The people still insist, and the LORD tells Samuel to give them a king.
chapters.8.lds: The Church lesson invites readers to consider Jesus Christ as their King. What does verse 17 say the people will become under a king?
chapters.9.summary: Saul, a tall young man of Benjamin, searches for his father’s lost donkeys. After three days he wants to turn back. His servant suggests asking a man of God in the nearby town. The servant also supplies the silver for a gift. The day before, the LORD told Samuel that a Benjamite would come. Samuel must anoint him as leader over Israel. Samuel seats Saul at the head of a feast and gives him a reserved portion. Saul says his tribe is the smallest and his family the least.
chapters.9.lds: Come, Follow Me connects Saul’s selection with a call to service. Who suggests visiting the man of God in verse 6?
chapters.10.summary: Samuel pours oil on Saul’s head and names three signs for the road home. All three happen, and God gives Saul another heart. The Spirit comes on him, and he prophesies among a band of prophets. He tells his uncle about the donkeys but not about the kingdom. Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpah and chooses by lot. The lot falls on Saul, who is hiding among the baggage. The people shout, “Long live the king!” Some men despise him, and he keeps silent.
chapters.10.lds: The Church lesson connects anointing and changed purpose with service by revelation. Where is Saul when the lot names him (verse 22)?
chapters.11.summary: Nahash the Ammonite surrounds Jabesh Gilead. He will make peace only if he may put out every right eye. The town sends messengers through Israel. Saul comes in from the field behind his oxen and hears the news. God’s Spirit comes on him, and he is very angry. He cuts up the oxen and sends the pieces as a summons. Israel gathers, and Saul breaks the Ammonite camp at dawn. He refuses to punish his critics, and the people renew the kingdom at Gilgal.
chapters.11.lds: The older manual studies Saul’s early leadership and the renewed kingdom. How does Saul answer the call for executions in verse 13?
chapters.12.summary: Samuel speaks to all Israel now that a king leads them. He asks whom he has cheated, oppressed, or taken a bribe from. The people answer that he has taken nothing. He reviews how the LORD rescued them each time they cried out. Still they asked for a king when the LORD was their king. If they and their king obey, it will go well. Samuel calls for thunder and rain at wheat harvest, and the people are afraid. He promises to keep praying for them and teaching them.
chapters.12.lds: The older manual studies Samuel’s final address and continued prayer for the people. What does Samuel ask the people to testify in verse 3?
chapters.13.summary: Jonathan attacks a Philistine post, and the Philistines gather a huge army. Israel’s men hide in caves and pits, and some cross the Jordan. Saul waits seven days at Gilgal for Samuel, as he was told. Samuel does not come, and the soldiers begin to leave. Saul offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel arrives at once and says Saul’s kingdom will not last. The LORD has sought a man after his own heart. Saul is left with six hundred men, and only he and Jonathan have swords.
chapters.13.lds: The Church lesson studies obedience under pressure. The older manual also reads the offering as unauthorized priesthood action. What three reasons does Saul give in verses 11–12?
chapters.14.summary: Jonathan and his armor bearer climb to a Philistine post alone. Jonathan says the LORD can save by many or by few. They kill about twenty men, and panic spreads through the Philistine camp. Saul joins the fight and puts a curse on anyone who eats before evening. Jonathan has not heard it and eats some honey. The hungry soldiers later eat meat with the blood. God gives Saul no answer, and the lot falls on Jonathan. Saul says he must die, but the people rescue him.
chapters.14.lds: The older manual studies Jonathan’s faith and the harmful effect of Saul’s oath. Why do the people refuse to let Jonathan die (verse 45)?
chapters.15.summary: Samuel gives Saul the LORD’s command to destroy Amalek completely. The reason given is Amalek’s attack on Israel after Egypt. Saul defeats them but spares King Agag and the best animals. The LORD tells Samuel he regrets making Saul king. Saul greets Samuel and claims he has obeyed. Samuel asks about the sheep he hears and says obeying is better than sacrifice. Saul admits he feared the people, and the LORD rejects him as king. Samuel kills Agag and never visits Saul again.
chapters.15.lds: Come, Follow Me asks why obedience matters more than making a religious display. Whom does Saul blame in verse 21, and what purpose does he claim?
chapters.16.summary: The LORD sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint a son of Jesse. Samuel admires the eldest, but the LORD looks at the heart. Seven sons pass by, and none is chosen. The youngest, David, is brought from the sheep, and Samuel anoints him. The LORD’s Spirit comes on David and leaves Saul. A troubling spirit torments Saul, and his servants seek a harp player. One of them recommends David. David enters Saul’s service, and his music gives the king relief.
chapters.16.lds: The Church lesson asks readers to consider a person's heart instead of outward appearance. What does David’s music do for Saul in verse 23?
chapters.17.summary: The Philistine champion Goliath challenges Israel to single combat for forty days. Saul and his army are afraid. David brings food to his brothers and hears the challenge. He tells Saul that the LORD saved him from a lion and a bear. Saul dresses David in his own armor, but David takes it off. He chooses five smooth stones and his sling. He tells Goliath that the battle is the LORD’s. One stone sinks into the giant’s forehead, and David cuts off his head.
chapters.17.lds: Come, Follow Me asks how trust in God can give courage during a hard task. Why does David take off Saul’s armor (verse 39)?
chapters.18.summary: Jonathan loves David and makes a covenant with him. He gives David his own robe, sword, and bow. Women sing that Saul has killed thousands and David ten thousands. Saul becomes angry and watches David from that day. Twice he throws a spear at him. He offers his daughter Merab, then gives her to another man. Michal loves David, and Saul asks a deadly bride price, hoping the Philistines kill him. David pays double, and Saul fears him even more.
chapters.18.lds: The Church lesson compares Jonathan’s support with Saul’s jealousy. What does Saul conclude from the women’s song in verse 8?
chapters.19.summary: Saul tells Jonathan and his servants to kill David. Jonathan defends David, and Saul swears he will not die. War returns, David wins again, and Saul throws his spear a third time. Saul’s men watch David’s house that night. Michal lowers David from a window and puts a household idol in his bed. David flees to Samuel at Ramah. Three groups of Saul’s messengers are overcome and begin to prophesy. Saul goes himself, and the Spirit overcomes him too.
chapters.19.lds: The older Church manual compares Samuel's group of prophets with later Church schools. How does Michal answer her father in verse 17?
chapters.20.summary: David asks Jonathan why Saul wants him dead. They agree on a test at the new moon feast. Jonathan asks David to show kindness to his family in the future. At the feast Saul notices David’s empty seat. He rages at Jonathan and says David blocks his way to the throne. Jonathan asks what David has done, and Saul throws a spear at him. Jonathan warns David with a signal of arrows in the field. They weep, swear friendship again, and part.
chapters.20.lds: What does Jonathan risk by protecting David from his father?
chapters.21.summary: David flees alone to the priests at Nob. He tells Ahimelech that the king sent him on secret business. He asks for bread, and the priest has only the holy bread. Ahimelech gives it once he hears the men have kept from women. David also takes Goliath’s sword, which was kept there. Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s chief herdsman, is present that day. David goes on to King Achish of Gath, where the servants recognize him. He pretends to be mad, and Achish sends him away.
chapters.21.lds: The older manual connects the bread account with Jesus’s later teaching about human need. What bread does the priest give David in verse 6?
chapters.22.summary: David hides in the cave of Adullam. His family and about four hundred troubled men join him. He leaves his parents with the king of Moab. Saul complains that his servants conspire against him. Doeg reports that Ahimelech gave David food and a sword. Ahimelech says David was the king’s loyal son-in-law. Saul orders the priests killed, and only Doeg obeys. Eighty-five priests and the town of Nob die, and Abiathar escapes to David.
chapters.22.lds: The older Church manual condemns Saul's attack on the priests. How do Saul’s guards respond to his order in verse 17?
chapters.23.summary: David asks the LORD twice and then rescues the town of Keilah from Philistines. Saul hears and prepares to trap him inside its gates. David asks through the priest’s ephod whether Keilah will hand him over. The answer is yes, so he leaves with six hundred men. Jonathan finds him in the wilderness and strengthens his trust in God. The people of Ziph tell Saul where David hides. Saul closes in around a mountain. A Philistine raid calls him away just in time.
chapters.23.lds: How does David respond when the town he saved may hand him over?
chapters.24.summary: Saul takes three thousand men to hunt David at En Gedi. He enters a cave alone, and David’s men are hiding deep inside. They say the LORD has given David his enemy. David cuts off a corner of Saul’s robe and then regrets even that. He will not harm the LORD’s anointed. Outside, he bows and shows Saul the cloth. Saul weeps and says David is more righteous than he is. He admits David will be king and asks mercy for his family.
chapters.24.lds: Come, Follow Me invites readers to study David's self-control and forgiveness. What does David hold up as proof in verse 11?
chapters.25.summary: Samuel dies, and Israel mourns him. David’s men have guarded the flocks of Nabal, a rich and harsh man. David asks for food at shearing time, and Nabal insults him. David arms four hundred men and swears to kill every male. Nabal’s wife Abigail hurries out with food and meets David on the road. She asks him not to shed blood he will later regret. David blesses her and turns back. Nabal dies ten days later, and David marries Abigail.
chapters.25.lds: The Church lesson studies restraint and forgiveness. It compares Abigail’s intervention with Jesus Christ. What does David thank Abigail for in verse 33?
chapters.26.summary: The people of Ziph again tell Saul where David is. Saul camps with three thousand men. David and Abishai slip into the camp at night and find Saul asleep. Abishai offers to pin him to the ground with one stroke. David forbids it and takes Saul’s spear and water jar. From a far hill he calls to Abner and to Saul. Saul admits he has played the fool and promises no more harm. David returns the spear, and each goes his own way.
chapters.26.lds: Come, Follow Me studies self-control. Restraint and continued separation occur together in the story. What does David tell Abner to look for in verse 16?
chapters.27.summary: David decides that Saul will one day kill him. He crosses to the Philistines with six hundred men and their families. King Achish of Gath gives him the town of Ziklag. Saul stops searching for him. David raids the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites to the south. He leaves no one alive and takes the livestock. He tells Achish that he has raided Judah. Achish believes David’s own people now hate him.
chapters.27.lds: The older manual links David’s raids with earlier commands to take the land. The raids also kill whole households. What reason does verse 11 give for the killing?
chapters.28.summary: The Philistines gather for war, and Achish expects David to fight for him. Samuel is dead, and Saul has driven mediums from the land. Saul is afraid, and the LORD gives him no answer. He disguises himself and visits a medium at Endor by night. He asks her to bring up Samuel. Samuel says the LORD has given the kingdom to David. Tomorrow Saul and his sons will die. Saul falls to the ground, and the woman persuades him to eat.
chapters.28.lds: The older manual says the speaker was not Samuel. The chapter itself repeatedly calls him Samuel. What danger does the woman name in verse 9?
chapters.29.summary: The Philistine armies gather at Aphek, and David marches at the rear with Achish. The Philistine commanders ask what these Hebrews are doing there. Achish says he has found no fault in David. The commanders are angry and demand that David be sent back. They quote the song about Saul’s thousands and David’s ten thousands. Achish apologizes and tells David to leave at dawn. David protests that he has done nothing wrong. He and his men return south in the morning.
chapters.29.lds: Why do the Philistine leaders distrust David, even though Achish trusts him?
chapters.30.summary: David returns to Ziklag and finds it burned by Amalekites. The wives and children are gone, and his men talk of stoning him. David finds strength in the LORD and asks whether to pursue. Two hundred men are too tired to cross the brook Besor. An abandoned Egyptian slave leads the rest to the raiders. David recovers every person and all the goods. Some men want to give the two hundred nothing. David rules that all share alike and sends gifts to Judah’s elders.
chapters.30.lds: Why does David share recovered goods with people who stayed behind?
chapters.31.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Jonathan and two of his brothers are killed. Archers wound Saul badly. He asks his armor bearer to kill him, and the man is afraid. Saul falls on his own sword, and the armor bearer does the same. The Philistines cut off Saul’s head and hang his body on Beth Shan’s wall. Men of Jabesh Gilead march all night and take the bodies down. They burn them, bury the bones, and fast seven days.
chapters.31.lds: How do the people of Jabesh Gilead honor Saul after his defeat?
